recipes.name: Slow Cooked Apple Brown Betty
ingredients_raw: 3 cups apples - peeled, cored and diced

steps.text: Place apples in a slow cooker.
Toss bread cubes, brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt together in a bowl; sprinkle over apples, then drizzle with melted butter.
Cover the slow cooker. Cook on Low until apples are tender, about 3 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooked Apple Brown Betty
raw_recipe.description: This slow-cooked apple brown Betty recipe combines apples, warm spices, and buttery bread cubes in a comforting dessert you can make in a slow cooker.

review.reviewBody: LOVED it! I did make some changes..I sprayed the inside of my crock pot with a little pam. I tossed the apples in 2 tsp of lemon juice and 1 tsp cinnamon...I used a 1 cup of crushed grahm cracker instead of the sliced bread..and I added one cup of chopped walnut to the crumb topping. WHAT A HIT!!! kids loved it...Top it off with vanilla ice cream and whipped cream!

1.20.21 Was getting a little dry, so I did add a bit of apple juice. After tasting, I also added more cinnamon and nutmeg (personal taste). I cooked this in my Instant Pot® using the slow cooker function on low, and it was done in about 2 hours. Pretty happy with the way this turned out.

This Apple Brown Betty is the closest I've found to the one I made weekly with my Grandma growing up in Mississippi. I make with these few changes. Today I used 2 Macintosh, 2 Granny Smith, and 1 Honeycrisp apples peeled and diced; 10 slices white bread cubed and tossed with 1/2 c. melted butter, 3/4 tsp cinnamon, 3/4 c. packed brown sugar, 1/8 tsp salt. I layered apples, bread, apples, bread in a 9 inch baking dish and then slowly poured half & half over the top just until I could see the cream rising in the sides of the dish. It was probably 1/2 cup or so, i never measure. Adding cream or milk takes care of the dryness that one reviewer mentioned. Cover dish with foil and bake at 350 for 30-45 minutes until apples are fork-tender. Remove foil and bake an additional 10 minutes until top is nicely browned. Remove from oven and let cool slightly. Serve warm with vanilla ice cream. Divine!

I used 4 apples (1 granny, 3 empire) and sliced right into crock pot. Added 2 tsp lemon juice and stirred it up. Mixed 1 cup cinnamon graham crackers (instead of bread) with 1/2 tsp vanilla + recipe ingredients. It was on high for 1 1/2 hours (small slices); smells and tastes great! **UPDATE** I doubled the recipe to bring to a meeting. I put the apples first, then the topping, then the SECOND layer of apples with its topping. This way all the apples have the cinnamon and sugar taste. Started the slow cooker at my house 1/2 hour on low, drove to the meeting, plugged it in again for an hour on low. Perfect! Not mushy, but next time I'll be cutting back on the butter to 3/4 stick because the apples all just swimming in butter at the bottom. (By using cinnamon graham crackers, no separate cinnamon spice is needed)

Oh my goodness. This is heavenly. My changes: 9 pieces of bread and 2 sheets (8 squares) of graham crackers that have been crumbled. No nutmeg. Instead I used a bit of apple pie spice. I did not layer bread mixture on top of apples. I mixed everything together and stireed about 4 times during cooking. Set on high for about 1 - 1 1/2 hours. Had it with a big spoonful of vanilla ice cream. Will make this very often for the family.

Pretty Easy. A good way to use up leftover breads. I used a couple slices raisin bread, a couple hamburger buns and 2 slices white bread.
(A little extra cinnamon too, because I love the aroma as it cooks). To make the topping a little more interesting a handful of large flake oatmeal was sprinkled on top,(which resulted in a lovely crunch)
Final hint...I took the lid off the crockpot after the first hour and finished cooking the final hour lid-less, which helped the top to be firm and crunchy, instead of soft and soggy. Will definitely do this recipe again.
Raymond just called...he REALLY LIKED THIS. Next day was even better he says.

Amazing! Just like bread pudding with apples. I took others advice by mixing all ingredients together and cooked on high for 1 1/2-2 hours. Also used part graham cracker and part bread. Will make again!

This recipe was wonderful! As recommended by others, I used 3 fugi apples, 1 granny smith, and 1 bosc pear. I also used graham crackers instead of bread and mixed 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract with the melted butter. It was a hit! Not a drop left at my son's cub scout Blue and Gold Banquet!!

Just made this tonight and it turned out great. My modifications: used 5 granny smith, 4 fuji apples, added vanilla extract, reduced to 1/2 cup brown sugar, used 10 slices of freshly baked cinnamon raisin bread from our local grocer's bakery, and added another 1/4 cup of butter. I mixed everything all together in the crock before setting. Delicious and easy; this one is a keeper.

I doubled this recipe and made it for a potluck at church tonight. After allowing it to cook as per the recipe, I tasted it and it was good but I felt like the apple to bread ratio was off, and I didn't have anymore fresh apples so I added a can of apple pie filling, about 1/8 teaspoon of ground ginger, and 1/4 tsp of salt and it was perfect. I used 1/2 Pepperidge Farms Light Style Soft Wheat bread and 1/2 Pepperidge Farms Very Thin 100% Whole Wheat Bread and I love the outcome! I gave my stars based on the original recipe! It was not as well received at church as I thought it would be, but I didn't complain about bringing it home for my family to finish!

I have been making this for over 15 yrs and it is always a hit. I use whatever leftover bread I happen to have on hand (italian and french are best as they are denser they hlod up better ). Be careful not to use very ripe apples as they create a runnier,thinner sauce. Otherwise the only difference is that I slice my cored apples into eighths (not diced) and cook for 4 hours. DELICIOUS!!
Great to quickly throw together. Will test against my oven baked recipe. Caramel or maple syrup drizzle tops it off well.
Don't know what I did wrong, but it came out like soggy bread.
I have not made this but am disappointed that the recipes for cooing in a slow cooker do not indicate what size is needed.
I added half a cup of maple syrup/water to create a bit of a sauce, it’s excellent. The only thing that’s not great is the type of bread I had, too heavy for this. Otherwise it’s super good.
I added a half cup of apples.

Good flavor. Not as moist as I was expecting. Seems to need more spice and some liquid, maybe 1/2 to 1 cup of cider. Going to do a variation for my next Family dinner, I'll let you know. Thank you and don't get me wrong, it tasted good!!!
It was excellent! I made it exactly per the recipe, merely adding chopped pecans. Do it! You'll love it.
This was great. When I read a review I want to know what THIS was like, not what changes you made. If you change it, post your own recipe and we will rate that one!
I like to make all your recipes exactly as shown except the sugar. I only used a 1/2 cup of brown sugar. I really loved it.
